summary: Solid-carbon thermal batteries for round-the-clock industrial heat and power.
editor_note: Industrial storage gets interesting when the battery is a hot block, not another electrochemical cell. Antora stores electricity as heat in carbon for process heat or steam-turbine power. POET confirms first energy delivery at Big Stone, but describes a 5 GWh project still being commissioned, not a completed system. The next test is repeatable heat economics and operating performance beyond this first large project.

sources.label: Antora delivery products and project workflow

product_evidence.claim: Antora describes charging by resistively heating insulated solid carbon up to 2,400°C, storing the heat for multiple days, and discharging to industrial processes or steam turbines.

The solutions page lists HeatCore process-heat delivery up to 375°C and a steam-turbine power block as available products; the technology page describes direct thermophotovoltaic conversion as a future product.
POET's May 2026 announcement describes Big Stone as a 5 GWh project entering commissioning after reaching first energy delivery in under 12 months, with full operation expected later in 2026.
The Big Stone customer announcement describes a long-term heat offtake agreement and an electricity rate enabling charging during surplus local energy production.
Antora's project offering includes site screening, electricity procurement, financing, installation, controls integration, and ongoing operation and maintenance.

market_context.primary_user: Industrial plant energy and project teams buying continuous process heat; Antora also markets steam-turbine power systems to data-center and grid customers.
market_context.differentiation: The offering combines modular carbon heat storage with heat-delivery equipment, power procurement, financing, and operations; the POET reference is a heat offtake project, not evidence of every marketed power application.
market_context.why_now: POET's first-energy and commissioning announcement, followed by the July 2026 Series C, makes construction completion and repeat-site operating results the next observable milestones.

risks.claim: First energy delivery is not full project commissioning. The reviewed announcements do not establish final completion, sustained output, or independently audited operating economics for Big Stone.
risks.basis: Antora's project page and POET's May 2026 announcement distinguish first energy from planned full operation later in 2026.

risks.claim: Repeat-site economics depend on local electricity rates, financing, integration, and heat demand; a published carbon storage temperature is not the delivered process temperature or proof of universal cost savings.
risks.basis: VentureDex editorial assessment of the technology specifications, delivery products, and the site-specific POET offtake arrangement.
